hints: Remember what nucleon number really means, it counts all the heavy particles in the nucleus, both protons and neutrons.
Find the proton number of technetium, Tc, from your Periodic Table. It is element 43.
Now just add those two parts together, protons plus the 56 neutrons given, to get the total mass.
walkthrough:
**Recall what nucleon number means**

Think of the nucleus as a bag of nucleons. That is just a fancy word for protons plus neutrons.

$$ \text{nucleon number (mass number)} = \text{protons} + \text{neutrons} $$

**Find the protons in technetium**

Every Tc atom has the same number of protons. Look up Tc in the Periodic Table and you will see its atomic (proton) number is 43.

$$ \text{protons in Tc} = 43 $$

**Add to get the answer**

This isotope has 56 neutrons, so just add them to the 43 protons.

$$ \text{nucleon number} = 43 + 56 = 99 $$
That gives the isotope $^{99}\text{Tc}$, a very well known isotope.

options.A: 43 is the proton number (atomic number) of Tc, not the nucleon number. It forgets to add the 56 neutrons.
options.B: 56 is just the number of neutrons given in the question. Nucleon number must include protons as well, so this is incomplete.
options.C: Correct and well done. Protons (43) + neutrons (56) = 99. This is the nucleon number, also called the mass number, of this Tc isotope.
options.D: 112 comes from doubling 56, as if neutrons = protons. But Tc does not have 56 protons, it has 43 protons, so this addition is wrong.
